paper_title: Let the Expert Stick to His Last Expert-Specialized Fine-Tuning for   Sparse Architectural Large Language Models
caption: Top Expert distribution for specific tasks. Shaded areas represent variance across layers. The figure shows that few experts handle most gate values, highlighting expert specialization for different tasks.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the normalized average gate value across different numbers of experts, ranging from 1 to 64 on a logarithmic x-axis labeled "Experts", with the y-axis representing "Normalized Average Gate Value" on a linear scale from 0.00 to 0.20. The plot displays seven distinct lines, each corresponding to a specific task or distribution: "Intent" (orange solid line), "Summary" (blue solid line), "Law" (yellow solid line), "Translation" (purple solid line), "Math" (gray solid line), "Code" (green solid line), and "Uniform" (dashed gray line). All lines begin at approximately 0.06–0.07 for 1 expert and show a general downward trend as the number of experts increases, with the "Uniform" line remaining nearly constant at approximately 0.015. The "Translation" line starts at approximately 0.20 and declines sharply to near zero by 64 experts. The "Intent" and "Summary" lines start near 0.06 and decrease gradually, while the "Law" and "Code" lines follow a similar pattern but remain slightly higher than "Intent" and "Summary". The "Math" line remains relatively flat near 0.04. The shaded areas surrounding the lines represent the variance across layers for each task.
